item.title: For the Vanua | Ra’s rise to test Grammar’s pride
item.description: RA High School’s remarkable Vodafone Super Deans under-18 campaign reaches its biggest test yet when it faces Southern Zone powerhouse Suva Grammar School in the semi-final at Churchill Park, Lautoka, this weekend. For Ra, this is no longer simply about a school chasing a place in the Deans final.
item.content:encoded:
RA High School’s remarkable Vodafone Super Deans under-18 campaign reaches its biggest test yet when it faces Southern Zone powerhouse Suva Grammar School in the semi-final at Churchill Park, Lautoka, this weekend.

For Ra, this is no longer simply about a school chasing a place in the Deans final.

It is about a rugby community beginning to believe.

The boys from Ra have emerged as the surprise package of the competition, knocking out traditional powerhouse and defending champions Ratu Kadavulevu School in the quarter-final to earn their place among the final four.

But their biggest strength could be what lies beyond the school gates. Ra rugby is enjoying a resurgence at provincial level.

The Ra Rugby Union recently secured the Vodafone Vanua Championship title and, with it, promotion to the Skipper Cup for the first time in its history.

Against Ra High will be a Grammar side accustomed to the big stage.

The Lions have the resources, experience, depth and structure that have made them one of the recognised powers of secondary school rugby. They also have unfinished business.

Grammar’s last Deans U18 title came in 2001 when they defeated Ratu Kadavulevu School 34-10.

Twenty-five years later, the Lions are again within two wins of the trophy.

Their latest step came with a convincing 23-7 victory over Ba Provincial Freebird Institute in the quarter-final, where their forwards laid the foundation before the backs finished the job.

Grammar will therefore enter the semi-final with confidence. But they will also know that Ra have already shown they cannot be judged by reputation or resources.

Ra may not possess the same traditional pedigree as Grammar, but it has belief, physicality and the growing support of an entire province behind it.

For the Ra players, every tackle and every carry will be watched by a community that has tasted success at provincial level and now wants its schoolboys to create another piece of history.

The winner will book a place in the Deans final. But for Ra, victory would mean something more. It would confirm that the province’s recent rugby breakthrough is not an isolated success.

It would be another sign that Ra rugby is moving forward, from the provincial field to the schoolboy stage.

Ra are no longer just playing for Ra High School but they are playing for the vanua of Ra.

item.title: From parents’ vision to the international stage
item.description: WHAT began as a vision among parents to give their daughters greater exposure has grown into an international opportunity for the under-15 Royale Rising Star from Nakoivalu Netball Academy. The team will make its first appearance at the International Netball Festival in Christchurch, New Zealand from August 26-28.
item.content:encoded:
WHAT began as a vision among parents to give their daughters greater exposure has grown into an international opportunity for the under-15 Royale Rising Star from Nakoivalu Netball Academy.

The team will make its first appearance at the International Netball Festival in Christchurch, New Zealand from August 26-28.

The team was formed by parents whose daughters have been playing club netball since they were 10 years old.

Academy founder Unaisi Ranavue said the idea was to bring the parents together and create an opportunity for the girls to experience international competition.

“The parents thought to come together to organise an international tour and to have an exposure for the International Netball Festival,” Ranavue said.

The team’s participation is also a milestone for the academy, which had previously only followed the tournament from afar.

“We’ve been hearing about it, but we’ve never been part of it,” she said.

“So, this is a milestone and a huge achievement for us to get registered and be part of the competition.”

The team is now preparing for the Christchurch challenge, with the players having completed strength and conditioning and core sessions before moving into court work.

Ranavue also said the experience would be about more than results, with the players gaining confidence and learning from competing at an international level.

The International Netball Festival is celebrating its 50th anniversary this year.

item.title: Fijiana name side for second Test
item.description: THE Vodafone Fijiana XV has named its starting side for Saturday’s second test against the Springbok women at Churchill Park in Lautoka, with several changes to the team that started the opening match. Karalaini Naisewa will start at prop, with Bitila Tawake(vice captain) and Keri Lawavou retaining the number two and three jerseys.
item.content:encoded:
THE Vodafone Fijiana XV has named its starting side for Saturday’s second test against the Springbok women at Churchill Park in Lautoka, with several changes to the team that started the opening match.

Karalaini Naisewa will start at prop, with Bitila Tawake(vice captain) and Keri Lawavou retaining the number two and three jerseys.

Jade Coates starts at lock alongside Karavaki Lutumaibau, while Nunia Daunimoala and Adi Salaseini Railumu retain their places in the loose forwards.

Merewairita Neivoha moves into the number seven jersey, with Adi Salaseini Railumu at number eight.

Kolora Lomani continues as captain at scrum-half, with Varanisese Qoro at fly-half.

At centre, Ruth Raketekete and Ivamere Rokowati will line up together, while Atelaite Buna and Adi Vani Buleki start on the wings.

Litiana Vueti retains the fullback position.

The changes come after Fijiana suffered a 55-12 defeat to South Africa in the opening Test in Suva last Saturday.

Reserves; Selai Naliva, Elesi Saukuru, Tiana Robanakadavu, Vilisi Tivalele, Sereana Maragi, Evivi Senikarivi, Adi Salote Nailolo, Vasemaca Duva.

Fijiana coach Willie Walker will be looking for a response from his players after identifying discipline, ball retention and defence as key areas for improvement following the first Test.

item.title: Lelean chase deans glory after 12 years wait
item.description: LELEAN Memorial School will be hoping to end a 12-year wait for the Vodafone Deans Trophy as the Under-18 side continues its campaign in the semi-final this Saturday, August 15, at HFC Bank Stadium. The competition has reached another decisive stage where the side will face Nasinu Secondary School in the semi-finals.
item.content:encoded:
LELEAN Memorial School will be hoping to end a 12-year wait for the Vodafone Deans Trophy as the Under-18 side continues its campaign in the semi-final this Saturday, August 15, at HFC Bank Stadium.

The competition has reached another decisive stage where the side will face Nasinu Secondary School in the semi-finals.

Lelean last won the Deans trophy in 2014, and the current U18 side now has the opportunity to revive the school’s campaign for national honours.

With a place in the finals at stake, Lelean will be determined to make the opportunity count and move a step closer to ending the long wait.

The Deans Trophy has long been one of the biggest prizes in Fiji Secondary School rugby, and Lelean has a proud history in the competition having won the Deans Trophy 14 times.

A win against Nasinu would put Lelean into the national final and within a touching distance of the first Deans title since 2014.

The 12-year gap between titles has added significance to the campaign, with the players carrying hopes of a school eager to see the trophy return to Davuilevu.

The U18 side will now turn its attention to the semi-final against Nasinu Secondary School, a side who is also determined to book its place in the final after being denied the title in the last two years.

YESTERDAY’S inter-house athletics meet at HFC Bank Stadium marked another important chapter for Holy Trinity Primary School, as students took to the track to compete for their respective houses.

The event brought plenty of energy and excitement, but for the school, the significance went beyond the day’s results. Teachers and organisers used the competition as an opportunity to encourage participation, build confidence and assess the potential within the school.

item.title: Holy Trinity lays foundation for next generation
item.description: HOLY Trinity Primary School is looking beyond yesterday’s inter-house athletics competition at HFC Bank Stadium, using the event as an important starting point in its long-term plan to identify and develop young athletes. For the first time, Year one and Year two students were included as official competitors at the school’s inter-house meet, giving the youngest athletes an opportunity to experien
item.content:encoded:
HOLY Trinity Primary School is looking beyond yesterday’s inter-house athletics competition at HFC Bank Stadium, using the event as an important starting point in its long-term plan to identify and develop young athletes.

For the first time, Year one and Year two students were included as official competitors at the school’s inter-house meet, giving the youngest athletes an opportunity to experience competition and contribute points towards their respective houses.

Holy Trinity meet manager Aisake Kuruduadua said the decision was part of a deliberate effort to strengthen the school’s athletics development pathway.

“This year is the first time that we are actually involving our Year 1 and 2 to actually compete in the competition,” Kuruduadua said.

He said the students had previously participated only in informal running activities during breaks, but the school wanted to introduce them to competition at an earlier age.

Their inclusion means students can begin developing an understanding of competition while still in their first years of primary school.

“That is something we did new for this year which we think will actually motivate the students from Year 1 as they go along before they actually compete,” Kuruduadua said.

For Holy Trinity, the bigger objective is not simply to produce winners at an inter-house meet, but to create a pathway where promising athletes can continue developing as they move through the school system.

Early participation can give students the opportunity to build confidence, learn the fundamentals of competition and gradually progress to district meets and higher levels of athletics.

Kuruduadua said Holy Trinity had already built a strong reputation in athletics, with the commitment of teachers and parents contributing significantly to the school’s success.

He said maintaining that tradition would require continued support as the school works to develop the next generation.

Parents, in particular, remain an important part of the pathway, with Kuruduadua encouraging greater recognition of the opportunities athletics can provide beyond the school environment.

item.title: Namuka finish Pool A campaign with win
item.description: NAMUKA closed their Pool A campaign on a high, defeating Moce by 47 runs in the Super 8 Championship at Albert Park yesterday. Batting first, Namuka posted 178 runs before being bowled out, setting Moce a target of 179 for victory.
item.content:encoded:
NAMUKA closed their Pool A campaign on a high, defeating Moce by 47 runs in the Super 8 Championship at Albert Park yesterday.

Batting first, Namuka posted 178 runs before being bowled out, setting Moce a target of 179 for victory.

Moce struggled to build momentum in the chase and were eventually bowled out for 131, handing Namuka a convincing 47-run win.

Namuka all-rounder Jake Bernard Cakacaka credited God and the supporters who stood behind the team throughout the match.

“Thank God for the game we played today and for the unwavering support,” Cakacaka said.

While pleased with the result, Cakacaka believes the side still has areas to improve, particularly in the field.

“We need to improve our fielding. There is still plenty of room for improvement, and we will try our best to keep getting better,” he said.

Namuka’s 178-run total gave the team a solid platform before their bowlers took control of the chase.

Moce needed 179 runs but struggled to build partnerships and eventually lost all their wickets for 131.

Cakacaka said the team was grateful for the support they received during the match.

“We are thankful for all the support,” he said.

The 47-run victory provided Namuka with a strong finish to their Pool A campaign and showed the team’s ability to perform with both bat and ball.

After putting a competitive total on the board, Namuka’s bowlers maintained pressure throughout the Moce innings and ensured the target remained out of reach.

For Cakacaka and his teammates, however, the victory is also an opportunity to identify areas that need work.

The all-rounder said the team would continue to focus on improving its performance as the competition progresses.

Namuka can take plenty of confidence from the win, but their fielding remains an area they want to sharpen.

The victory gives the side positive momentum as the Super 8 Championship enters its decisive stage, with Namuka looking to build on yesterday’s performance and continue its push for the title.

item.title: Rewa FC pick up crucial three points in Ba
item.description: Rewa FC secured a much-needed victory over Tupapa Maraerenga FC to keep their OFC Men’s Champions League dreams alive on home soil in Ba. Both sides were looking to bounce back from opening day defeats, with Rewa in particular keen to get their first points on the board, as they tried to take advantage of a passionate home crowd in warm and humid conditions.
item.content:encoded:
Rewa FC secured a much-needed victory over Tupapa Maraerenga FC to keep their OFC Men’s Champions League dreams alive on home soil in Ba.

Both sides were looking to bounce back from opening day defeats, with Rewa in particular keen to get their first points on the board, as they tried to take advantage of a passionate home crowd in warm and humid conditions.

They started by far the brighter side, but despite their efforts struggled to trouble Tupapa Maraerenga’s defence in the early stages. Setareki Hughes and Don Keana were leading the charge for Rewa, but goalkeeper Tahiri Elikana remained largely untested.

Ramzan Khan stood out as one of Rewa’s top performers as they grew into the game and he came closest to opening the scoring with a rasping effort from distance that Elikana did well to tip onto the crossbar.

Josaia Sela was next to create a good chance and should have done better with the opportunity. The forward worked his way in-field from the left-hand channel, cutting inside and firing wide of the near post when he should have hit the target.

Tupapa worked hard to try and catch their opponents on the break, but struggled to take advantage of Rewa’s high defensive line.

It was little surprise when the deadlock was finally broken and even less surprise that it came via the excellent Khan. The midfielder unleashed another long-range effort and this one proved too good for Elikana, flying past the ‘keeper and into the top corner to give Rewa a half-time lead.

Tupapa had struggled to get a foothold in the first-half but within seconds of the restart they were level. Catching the Rewa defence cold, Tremaine Rimene-Albrett was played clean through by Honoura Maraetefau and he made no mistake, sliding the ball past the on-rushing Epeli Loaniceva.

Parity wouldn’t last long however, as Rewa hit back almost immediately. Don Keana showing his pace and power down the right, beating his man and crossing for Joseph Athale. The New Caledonian initally lost control of the ball, but reacted quickest in the box to scramble home from a few yards out.

Rewa were determined to try and press home their advantage having regained the lead. Athale continued to look dangerous, whilst Setareki Hughes came close with a trademark left-footed effort that narrowly flew past the far post.

Hughes would have another, similar opportunity shortly after and it led to Rewa’s third goal. Substitute Merrill Nand’s corner was cleared only as far as Hughes and after creating space himself, he curled his effort into the far corner to double Rewa’s lead.

Brazilian Lucas Santos was brought on in the final twenty minutes for Rewa and the forward looked dangerous from the outset, including a testing drive that goalkeeper Elikana held at the second attempt.

A fourth would arrive for Rewa with just five minutes remaining, when Josaia Sela met an excellent cross from the left from Kavaia Rawaqa – his initial header was well saved by Elikana but Sela reacted to bury the rebound.

Tupapa worked hard to the end and were rewarded for doing so with a late consolation. Honoura Maraetefau taking advantage of a slack pass from goalkeeper Loaniceva, picking up the ball and firing home as it finished 4-2.

Rewa FC: 4 (Ramzan KHAN 40′, Joseph ATHALE 48′, Setareki HUGHES 67′, Josaia SELA 85′)

Tupapa Maraerenga FC: 2 (Tremaine RIMENE-ALBRETT 47′, Honoura MARAETEFAU 90+4′)
